## Incident Report — 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

**Capture window:** 2024-09-04 17:32–18:32 UTC (~1 hour), 5,091 packets, LAN segment 172.17.0.0/24.

### Infected Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 172.17.0.99 |
| MAC address | 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-RNVO9AT |
| AD domain | bepositive.com (DC: WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19 / 172.17.0.17) |
| Logged-in user | afletcher (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString) |

Host identity is corroborated by DHCP request (option 12 hostname = DESKTOP-RNVO9AT, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4) and NBNS name registrations for the same hostname.

### Malware Family
**Koi Stealer** (aka Koi Loader/Koi Stealer). **Signature-confirmed** — Suricata/ET alert `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` fired 48 times against the same C2 IP/URI pair, corroborated by `ET INFO GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser 1` (POSTing directly to a raw IP with a spoofed old-IE user agent, no DNS lookup preceding it).

Behavioral traits observed align with the signature: encrypted/opaque POST bodies (`application/octet-stream`, `Content-Encoding: binary`) to a hardcoded IP literal, a spoofed legacy `MSIE 7.0`/Trident user agent, and a persistent ~60-90 second beacon interval (96 checkins over the hour) — no PE/EXE binary was observed transiting HTTP in this capture, consistent with credential/data exfiltration over an encrypted channel rather than a visible secondary payload drop.

### Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint:**
- `79.124.78.197:80` (TCP) — sole C2 IP, contacted directly with no prior DNS resolution (hardcoded)

**No malicious domains observed** — the infection communicates by IP literal only; all resolved domains in the capture (bepositive.com AD zone, Microsoft/MSN/Office telemetry, Adobe ARM update, Windows Update CRL/CT infrastructure) are legitimate.

**Malicious URLs / URIs (host 79.124.78.197):**
- `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` — initial gate/registration request (frame 2227, first contact 17:35:11 UTC)
- `POST /index.php` — encrypted registration payload upload; server replies with session token `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn`
- `POST /foots.php` — recurring encrypted beacon/exfil channel (96 occurrences, 17:35:07–18:31:53 UTC), body format `<cmd_id>|<bot_GUID>|...`, bot GUID observed: `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`, subid `qIOuKk7U`

**Transferred files / hashes:** None recoverable. No executable (PE/MZ header) was transferred over any HTTP object in the capture (verified via `--export-objects http` and a `file_data contains "MZ"` filter — no hits). All POST/response bodies to the C2 are opaque binary/encrypted blobs, so no SHA256 can be computed for a dropped payload from this evidence; only the beacon protocol strings above are recoverable in the clear.

### Supporting noise (not attributed to the infection)
Suricata also flagged internal SMBv1/NTLMSSP/Kerberos anomalies between 172.17.0.99 and the DC (172.17.0.17) — these are normal (if legacy/insecure) Windows domain-join/logon chatter, not malware indicators, and are noted only for completeness.
